questions.q: What specific problem does Ingress solve that the previous lesson identified with LoadBalancer Services?
options: Giving every externally facing app its own LoadBalancer Service means provisioning and paying for a separate cloud load balancer per app
LoadBalancer Services only work with TCP, never HTTP
LoadBalancer Services cannot use label selectors
LoadBalancer Services are not reachable from inside the cluster
questions.explain: Ingress lets many HTTP(S) routing rules share one entry point — typically fronted by a single LoadBalancer Service for the Ingress controller — instead of provisioning a dedicated cloud load balancer for every app.

questions.q: What happens if you create an Ingress resource in a cluster with no Ingress controller installed?
options: Kubernetes automatically installs ingress-nginx to satisfy it
The Ingress resource is rejected by the API server and cannot be created
Traffic is routed using the cluster's default NodePort instead
Nothing — the Ingress object is just a declarative description of rules, and nothing implements them without a controller running
questions.explain: An Ingress resource has no effect on its own. An Ingress controller (ingress-nginx, Traefik, a cloud-managed controller, etc.) has to be running in the cluster, watching for Ingress objects, and turning their rules into real routing.

questions.q: In an Ingress rule's path entry, what does backend.service point to?
options: A raw Pod IP address
An ordinary Kubernetes Service, which the Ingress sits in front of rather than replaces
A ConfigMap containing routing rules
A NetworkPolicy that permits the traffic
questions.explain: Ingress doesn't replace Services — each rule's backend.service still names a regular Service (commonly ClusterIP), and Ingress adds host/path-based routing in front of it.

questions.q: What is the purpose of ingressClassName in an Ingress resource's spec?
options: It sets the TLS certificate used for that host
It specifies the container image for the backend Pods
It defines which port the Service listens on
It tells Kubernetes which installed Ingress controller should handle that particular Ingress object
questions.explain: In clusters running more than one Ingress controller, ingressClassName picks which one is responsible for implementing a given Ingress resource's rules.

questions.q: How does TLS termination typically work at an Ingress?
options: Each backend Service decrypts its own HTTPS traffic independently
The Ingress controller decrypts HTTPS using a referenced kubernetes.io/tls Secret, then forwards plain HTTP to the backend Service
TLS is handled entirely by kube-proxy, with no involvement from the Ingress controller
TLS certificates must be baked into the container image rather than stored as a Secret
questions.explain: The Ingress spec's tls section references a secretName holding a kubernetes.io/tls Secret. The Ingress controller terminates HTTPS at that shared entry point and forwards plain HTTP on to the backend Service.
